rich_summary: This section describes the crucial moment leading to Bhishma’s fall on the tenth day of the Kurukshetra war. Sikhandin boldly challenges Bhishma, declaring he will slay him for the sake of the Pandavas. Arjuna supports the plan, promising to protect Sikhandin while he confronts the grandsire. Dhritarashtra anxiously asks Sanjaya how this encounter unfolded and who guarded Sikhandin. Sanjaya recounts Bhishma’s devastating prowess: he continues slaughtering Pandava forces by the thousands, appearing like the god of destruction. Arjuna then charges the battlefield like a roaring lion, scattering the Kuru army. Alarmed, Duryodhana urges Bhishma to save the collapsing forces. Bhishma responds by recalling his vow to slay ten thousand warriors daily and declares that this day he will either kill the Pandavas or die, preparing for a final, fateful clash.

highlight_spans.why: Sikhandin’s fierce vow to kill Bhishma sets the emotional and narrative stakes for the coming confrontation.
Arjuna urges Sikhandin forward and promises protection, revealing the Pandava strategy to bring down the otherwise invincible Bhishma.
Description of Bhishma slaughtering thousands emphasizes his near-mythic power and the desperation of the Pandavas.
Bhishma’s declaration that he will either slay the Pandavas or die fulfills his warrior’s vow and foreshadows his imminent fall.

top_scenes.scene_text: Sikhandin stands before Bhishma on the battlefield, bow drawn and eyes blazing, while Arjuna positions his chariot behind him with Krishna as charioteer.
Arjuna charges across Kurukshetra roaring like a lion, arrows streaming from his bow as terrified Kuru warriors scatter before him.
Bhishma, radiant and unstoppable in the midst of battle, releases torrents of arrows while Duryodhana pleads with him to save the collapsing Kuru army.
